# Plugin sync
English | 中文
**Your plugins follow you. Nothing to re-find on the next machine.**

The profile's plugin list, versions and configuration live in your own private
GitHub repository — n

ot someone's cloud. Backups happen as you change plugins;
a new machine pulls the manifest, shows yo

u the difference, and restores what
you pick. Plugins installed from a local directory come back as

source, secrets
never travel, and every download is checksummed before it is written.

Screenshots use fictional sample data (`octocat`, `workstation`); nothing from a
real account or mac

e fictional sample data (`octocat`, `workstation`); nothing from a
real account or machine is shown.
## What it does

- **Inventory** — every profile bundle that is not shipped with the installation:
name, version, ena

blement, installation source, and the row ids it declares.
- **Where it came from** — the repository

each plugin was really installed from:
the git remote of a local checkout first, the package's own

`repository` field
second, including the subdirectory of a monorepo. Unknown stays unknown.
- **Conf

iguration** — the profile's override layer for those rows, with
credential-shaped values replaced by

`<redacted>` before anything leaves the
machine. Environment references (`apiKeyEnv`) are kept, bec

ause they name a
secret instead of containing one.
- **Source backup** — a bundle installed from a l

ocal directory (`link:`/`file:`)
has no registry version to reinstall from, so its sources are commi

tted to the
same private repository as real files, one commit per push, browsable on
GitHub. Restore

downloads, verifies the SHA-256, writes the files and links the
directory.
- **Restore** — missing

bundles, version replacement, configuration writes and
enablement toggles, grouped and opt-in. Nothi

ng is applied without your click,
and each result reports what the Host actually did.
- **Updates**

— know when a plugin's origin publishes something newer than what
is installed. One click upgrades i

t here; local checkouts are left to you.
- **Cleanup** — per-plugin sync switch (this machine only),

and a *Prune backup*
action that removes entries — optionally their source files — from the shared

manifest.
- **Push** — after a plugin change (30 s debounce) and on demand.
- **Pull** — on a timer

and on demand; the difference is shown, never applied by
itself.
## Install

The repository is an installable bundle (`package.json` declares `dsh.bundle`).
Point the Harness pl

ugin manager at this directory or the GitHub repository,
then reload the page: **Settings → Plugin s

t this directory or the GitHub repository,
then reload the page: **Settings → Plugin sync** appears.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Requires DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x (the `settings.section`, `ctx.locale`,
`ctx.pluginManager`, `ctx.con
figEditor` and `ctx.credentials` contracts).
## Sign in

The page offers both GitHub steps as pre-filled links, so nothing has to be typed
from memory. The d

efault data repository is **`dsh-plugin-sync-data`**; the bare
name `dsh-plugin-sync` stays reserved
for the plugin's own public repository.
1. **① Create the private repository** → `github.com/new?name=dsh-plugin-sync-data&visibility=privat

e`; click Create (an empty repository, no README).
[该节后续省略]
## What lands in the repository
`dsh-plugin-sync.json` at the repository root:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Local sources are stored as real files under `snapshots/<name>/<version>/`,
written through the Git

Data API so a push is **one commit** and the repository
stays readable: you can open a plugin's sour

ce on GitHub, see the diff between
two backups, and search it. Files are content-addressed, so an un

changed file
costs no upload. Removed files are deleted in the same commit; the executable bit
is pr

file
costs no upload. Removed files are deleted in the same commit; the executable bit
is preserved.

Which files: those listed by the package's `files` field, plus `package.json`,
`cordis.patch.yml`, `

locale/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`, the icon and the READMEs.
`node_modules`, `.git`, `.env*`, logs and

symlinks never are. A file above 1 MiB
or a snapshot above `maxSnapshotBytes` refuses the whole sna

pshot instead of
uploading a truncated one.
## Security notes

- **Routes accept a loopback browser only.** `/state` and `/api` require the
custom header `x-dsh-pl

ugin-sync: 1` (which forces a CORS preflight the route
never answers, so another origin cannot send

it), refuse any peer that is not
`127.0.0.1`/`::1`, and reject an `Origin` outside loopback or a bro

wser
`Sec-Fetch-Site` of `cross-site`. A plain `curl` still needs the header, and a
web page cannot

add it. They are **not** behind the Harness session login: keep
Harness on loopback.
- **The token i

s bound to the host that validated it.** Login calls `GET /user`
against an HTTPS base (plain HTTP o

nly for loopback), and the base is stored in
the credential record beside the token. Every later req

uest uses that stored
base, so changing a setting can never route the token elsewhere; switching API

hosts requires pasting the token again.
- **Nothing secret is published.** Redaction is two-layered

: credential-shaped
key names *and* credential-shaped values (`ghp_…`, `github_pat_…`, `sk-…`,
`xox…

`, `AKIA…`, PEM private keys) become `<redacted>`. Environment references
such as `apiKeyEnv` stay,

because they name a secret instead of containing one.
- **Sources are scanned and refused.** A file

that matches a credential shape
stops the upload and names the file, so a token pasted into a plugin

can never
reach the repository.
- **The manifest carries no local paths.** A linked bundle's absolu

te path is
replaced by `local:<name>`; restore uses the source backup. Repository paths
(`manifestPa

th`, `snapshotsPath`, a snapshot's own path) are validated against
`..`, absolute forms and backslas

hes, and every restored file is checksummed and
path-checked before it is written.
- **Provenance ne

ver carries credentials.** A git remote such as
`https://user:token@github.com/o/r.git` is normalize

d to a plain URL before it
is stored.
- **Only expected sources install.** Apply accepts a `github:`

is refused with `INSTALL_REFUSED` / `SOURCE_MISSING`. Updates are
pinned to the exact version that w

as detected.
